charts.title: Bank Rate

variants.name: Simple Taylor rule
variants.formula: i = 0.5 + π + 0.5(π − 2) + 0.5y. Taylor (1993), with a 0.5% neutral real rate; no smoothing.

lines.name: Simple Taylor rule, from Bank of England projections

variants.name: Contemporaneous Taylor-type rule (Bank)
variants.formula: i<sub>t</sub> = 0.85i<sub>t−1</sub> + 0.15(3 + 0.375(π<sup>E</sup><sub>t</sub> − 2) + 1.5(π<sup>N</sup><sub>t</sub> − 2) + 0.5y<sub>t</sub>), with π<sup>E</sup> and π<sup>N</sup> energy and non-energy CPI inflation.

lines.name: Contemporaneous Taylor-type rule (Bank), from Bank of England projections

variants.name: Forward-looking Taylor-type rule (Bank)
variants.formula: i<sub>t</sub> = 0.85i<sub>t−1</sub> + 0.15(3 + 1.5(π<sub>t+5|t</sub> − 2) + 0.5y<sub>t+5|t</sub>), using projections for five quarters ahead.

lines.name: Forward-looking Taylor-type rule (Bank), from Bank of England projections

variants.name: Forward-looking first-difference rule (Bank)
variants.formula: Δi<sub>t</sub> = 0.1(π<sub>t+3|t</sub> − 2) + 0.1(ΔGDP<sub>t+3|t</sub> − 0.375), using projections for three quarters ahead (quarterly GDP growth, measured from a 0.375% trend).

lines.name: Forward-looking first-difference rule (Bank), from Bank of England projections

charts.note: Dashed amber and teal lines are the market-implied path of Bank Rate each forecast was conditioned on (quarterly averages, plotted mid-quarter). The navy line is the chosen policy rule applied to the Bank of England's latest projections, starting from today's Bank Rate (quarterly; i = Bank Rate, π = CPI inflation, y = output gap, all %). The Bank's three rules are from its November 2025 MPR (Annex 1), with i* = 3%. The Bank publishes its output gap by year (interpolated to quarters) and energy only as its contribution to CPI inflation in Q4, from which energy and non-energy inflation are worked out. Unlike the Bank's own simulations, the projections don't respond to the different rate path.

charts.title: Crude oil prices
charts.note: Spot prices, weekly; the EIA updates weekly, so the latest can be a week old. Dashed lines are the market prices the forecasters assumed (quarterly averages of futures prices at their cut-off dates, plotted mid-quarter), not forecasts of their own. The Bank of England's oil path can't be republished (licensed data).
